text: The registry version answer carries, for the version in force and for each other version of the package: the package code, the version label, the state, the valid-from date, the valid-to date, the checksum of the artifact, the artifact reference, the row count and the test result; it carries the rows of a version only while that version is in force. The decision-log item carries the entry id, case id, decision code, rule id, rule version, final call, decided time, inputs reference, actions and chainVerified, with the actions holding the second rule, the intermediate state, the route state reached, the plan reference, the plan status and its date. The checksum is the SHA-256 of the stored artifact (the generated DRL with the workbook it came from).
why: The context pack and the P7 FSD and TSD name the state of a version, the checksum check, the rule and the version on an entry, and give no field list for either answer; the legacy story gives the monolith Java shapes and not a wire shape.

text: The page size of the decision-log read is 50 items by default and the ingest retries three times before the record is dead-lettered; both are settings of the service and not business values. The login of the service follows the one-login-per-service pattern of DP-02 and is taken from the database platform story rather than written here.
why: No source in the read set fixes a page size, a retry count or a login name, and the pattern tables name the shape of each and not its value.

text: One ledger entry is written per case, business date and rule identity. A move that runs two rules in one transaction writes one entry, with the rule of the final call in rule_id, and the second rule with the intermediate state and the state reached in the actions payload; the plan reference, the plan status and its date travel inside the inputs snapshot and the actions as values of the record. A version that is not in force, or a record whose checksum does not recompute, is refused with HTTP 409 and an RFC 9457 problem body naming the package code, the version label and its state, with no rows and no new message identifier; MSG-P7-003, MSG-P7-009, MSG-P7-012, MSG-P7-008, MSG-P3-027, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 keep their legacy text.
why: The legacy story moves the state twice in one transaction and writes an entry for each move while the record carries one rule and one version, and no source writes a message for a refused version, which did not exist in the monolith.

text: The plan-status read, the live answer, the stored plan status with its date, the route state, the task, the durable timer, the rights and the scope check stay with rwb-integration, rwb-case and rwb-access under RWB-P2-E2002-CON, RWB-P3-E2002-APP and RWB-P4-E2002-APP. The rwb-decision slice of RWB-E2-002 is the version of package RESTRUCTURE that was in force for the business date, and the record of the route moves the plan status caused; the plan-status endpoint of the legacy story is not served here and is consumed only through RWB-P2-E2002-CON at display time. The screen is one gateway-bff composite route that calls this service for the entries and rwb-case for the header.
why: The legacy key is filed under P2 Integration and owns the plan-status endpoint, while the plan places this APP slice in rwb-decision, whose ownership rows carry no plan-status path; the boundaries then have to be stated rather than inferred from the legacy module.

text: The platform H rows, the two C rows and the outbox and inbox objects that the patterns add are held by the platform, contract and registry stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which keep the plan value Depends on (build) = None and Contract dependencies = RWB-P2-E2002-CON. The story therefore builds against the published contracts, their fakes and the platform release train, stays Day 1 in its lane, and records the pattern rows in section 13 so the sequencing is visible.
